meta.title: Vietnam's Stunning Imperial City (Hue in 1 Day)
meta.description:
Join Madison and Ivan as they uncover the wonders of Hue, Vietnam's Imperial City, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Get ready to immerse yourself in the history of emperors, admire breathtaking architecture, and indulge in the flavors of culinary innovation. Don't forget to subscribe for more travel adventures!

Tour from Da Nang (or Hoi An) to Hue by Hai Van Tunnel, the longest tunnel in Southeast Asia. Visit Lang Co - Lap An Lagoon considered one of the most beautiful lagoons in the world! We visit the beautiful Mausoleum of Emperor Khai Dinh, Thien Mu Pagoda the oldest Pagoda in Hue, and the Imperial City where we visit the forbidden city! We also visit a pearl & a food souvenir shop.

For Ivan, a former NASA engineer, it is creating an engineering product that will change the world! Travel and food are two of our biggest passions, so on this channel we will be traveling the world, and staying awhile to experience what life is actually like living other places. comments.author: @elepfly
comments.text: The building with vibrant colors that you love is actually reconstructed recently as the original palace was destroyed completely during the war. As you can see, the weather in Hue is extremely hot and humid, so all of the color pigments will soon deteriorate, and the buildings then become just gray and brown which makes it look much older than it is, just like what you think of Khai Dinh's tomb. However, you can imagine a Hue citadel in its golden age, with all of those palaces, temples, and tombs all painted and ornated in a yellow, red, and blue theme of colors.

comments.author: @letsmadventure
comments.text: That makes so much more sense haha. I was wondering how many of the buildings in the citadel were still so vibrant! It is really cool to get to see it as it looked back in its prime though, but I definitely also enjoy the faded look of Khai Dinh's tomb where you can really see the history. It is so special that we get to see both in Hue! Thanks so much for the info!
